patterns.label: like / don't like - likes / doesn't like
patterns.rule: don't = do not, doesn't = do not (he/she/it)

patterns.label: Do you like...? / Does he like...?
examples: Do you like chocolate? Yes, I do. No, I don't.
Does he like chocolate? Yes, he does. No, he doesn't.
Does she like rice? Yes, she does.

patterns.label: So do I / Neither do I
examples: They like rice. - So do I.
They don't like rice. - Neither do I.
I like popcorn. - So do I.
I don't like soda. - Neither do I.
patterns.rule: Agree with a positive statement using So do I. Agree with a negative statement using Neither do I.

easy.why: He, she and it take likes.

core.why: Emma = she, so the verb takes -s.
Questions about he/she start with Does.

core.sentence: Do you like fries? - Yes, I ___.
core.why: Short answers repeat the helper verb: do.
A positive statement is agreed with So do I.

challenging.sentence: Emma and Leo ___ cookies, and Coco ___ them too.
challenging.why: Two people take like; one animal takes likes.

challenging.sentence: Ben doesn't like fruit. - ___ do I.
challenging.why: A negative statement is agreed with Neither do I.
After Does the verb loses its -s.
Neither is always followed by nor.
So echoes the helper verb, which is do here.

challenging.sentence: She likes rice, but she ___ like soup.
challenging.why: She takes doesn't, even in a contrast sentence.

easy.text: Dear diary, today is our class party. There is a lot of food. I like apples and popcorn. My friend Ben does not like fruit. He likes candy and soda. He is eating three cookies now. I am eating a banana. Then we play a game.

core.text: Dear diary, today is our class party and there is so much food on the table. I like fruit, so I am eating an apple and some grapes. My friend Ben doesn't like fruit at all. He only likes unhealthy snacks. He is eating a lot of candy and chocolate, and he is drinking soda. He says vegetables are boring. I think he is wrong. After lunch our teacher gives us popcorn, and everyone likes popcorn. Then it is time to go home.

questions.q: What does the writer eat first?

challenging.text: Dear diary, today is our class party and the long table is full of food. I like fruit, so I start with an apple and some grapes. My friend Ben doesn't like fruit at all; he says it is boring and it takes too long to eat. He only likes unhealthy snacks. By two o'clock he has eaten a lot of candy and chocolate, and he is drinking his second soda. Our teacher says, Ben, try some vegetables. Ben smiles but he doesn't take any. Later she brings out a big bowl of popcorn and suddenly everyone is happy. Even Ben. Popcorn is a vegetable, right? he asks. Nobody answers.

questions.q: Why does Ben say he doesn't like fruit?
options: It is boring and slow to eat
questions.answer: It is boring and slow to eat

questions.q: Find a word in the text that means 'not healthy'.
What does Ben's question at the end suggest?
options: He wants to believe popcorn is healthy
He wants to be a teacher
questions.answer: He wants to believe popcorn is healthy

questions.q: Which sentence shows that Ben eats a lot?
options: By two o'clock he has eaten a lot of candy
questions.answer: By two o'clock he has eaten a lot of candy

easy.text: All fruit comes from plants. Plants need water and sun. A tomato is a fruit. Tomatoes grow on vines. Some vines grow on big farms. Some vines grow in a small garden. Watermelon is a fruit too. Watermelons are very heavy, so they stay on the ground.

questions.q: Why do watermelons stay on the ground?

core.text: All fruit comes from plants, and plants need water and sun to grow. A tomato is a fruit, and many people are surprised by this. Tomatoes grow on vines. They can grow on big farms, and they can also grow in a small garden at home. Grapes and watermelons grow on vines too, but watermelons stay on the ground because they are very heavy. Apples and bananas are different: they grow on trees.

questions.q: What is surprising about a tomato?

challenging.text: All fruit comes from plants, and every plant needs water and sun to grow. A tomato is a fruit, which surprises many people because we usually put it in salads. Tomatoes grow on vines. Some vines cover whole fields on big farms; others climb a small frame in a garden at home. Grapes and watermelons grow on vines as well, but watermelons stay on the ground: they are too heavy to climb. Apples and bananas are different. They grow on trees, and most banana trees like hot weather, so you will not find them in cold countries. There are apple trees in many places around the world, and some may grow close to your home.

questions.q: What weather do banana trees like?
Why do watermelons stay on the ground?
options: They are too heavy to climb
questions.answer: They are too heavy to climb

questions.q: Find a word in the text that means 'large areas of land for growing food'.
What does the last sentence suggest to the reader?
options: You might find an apple tree near you
questions.answer: You might find an apple tree near you

tasks.prompt: Listen and repeat: I like cookies.
Listen and repeat: I don't like soda.
Say one true sentence about food. Use: I like ___ or I don't like ___.
Do you like popcorn? Answer with a full sentence.
Say the food chant: Cookies, candy, soda, rice. I like rice. It is very nice!

core.model: Do you like chocolate? Yes, I do. Does your friend like chocolate? No, she doesn't.

tasks.prompt: Ask and answer: Do you like fruit? Then answer in a full sentence.
Ask and answer: Does your friend like candy?
Look at the snack table. Say what you like and what you don't like. Use at least three food words.
Your friend says: I like popcorn. Agree with So do I. Then your friend says: I don't like soda. Agree with Neither do I.
Read the Snack Bar dialogue with two voices: you are Mia, then you are Leo.

challenging.model: On my plate I have rice, tomatoes and an apple. My sister likes tomatoes, and so do I. My brother doesn't like fruit, and neither do I, so we share the rice.

tasks.prompt: Speak for 60 seconds: My Snack Plate. Say what is on your plate, who in your family likes it, and one thing you agree about with So do I or Neither do I.
Compare two snacks. Use healthy, unhealthy, sweet and good for you.
Explain where fruit grows. Use tree, vine, ground and farm.
Answer three follow-up questions in full sentences: What do you eat for breakfast? Does your family like vegetables? What snack is good for you?
You are at the Snack Bar. Order food, say what you don't like, and agree with the server twice.

core.template: Dear diary, today I eat ___ at school. I like ___ but I don't like ___. My friend ___ likes ___.

challenging.prompt: Write a 5-sentence snack diary about today. Include: one food you like, one food you don't like, a sentence about a friend using like or likes, one So do I or Neither do I sentence, and one sentence about where fruit grows.
checklist: One So do I or Neither do I

speechScoring.provider: browser Web Speech API (free, no key, no server)
speechScoring.unsupportedFallback: record and self-assess with the 3-point rubric

scoring.matchRule: exact after normalisation, or Levenshtein distance <= 1 for words of 5+ letters

bands.message: Good - I heard most of it. Try once more for full marks.
Keep going - here are the words I heard.

scoring.neverShow: a numeric percentage or a pronunciation grade
scoring.privacy: Browsers may send audio to their own speech service. Show a one-line notice before the first recording.
